pathway.title: Alkermes plc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - The leverage step-up is the main credit constraint. The company moved from net cash of USD 388.57 million at year-end 2025 to net debt of USD 866.42 million, and the 5.93x ratio uses reported EBITDA that carries acquisition costs and only part-year LUMRYZ. The issuer's adjusted EBITDA for nine months 2026 is USD 339.54 million, 15.63% above a year earlier, so reported leverage probably overstates run-rate leverage, but no adjusted last-twelve-months figure can be built. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-03_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation G1; calculation G2

- Liquidity is comfortable in the near term but rests on cash alone. Cash and equivalents of USD 631.31 million cover the USD 164.19 million of principal due before 2031 by 3.85x, investments add USD 156.26 million, and no committed facility is described, so any shortfall would have to be met from cash. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation G6

- The refinancing wall sits in 2031 and follows the expiries. Principal of USD 1,347.56 million, 89.14% of the total, is due in 2031, after VIVITROL's last listed patent expires in 2029 and the Janssen royalties end in 2030; these two exposures were 31.87% of nine-month 2026 revenue. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2025-12-31_alks-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_alks-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation G5; calculation G6

- Margins are under pressure from deductions and cost growth. The adjusted EBITDA margin was 24.80% in nine months 2026 against 26.91% a year earlier, a fall of 2.11 percentage points, and 25.01% in Q3 against 30.83%, a fall of 5.83 percentage points, while sales deductions took 46.6% of gross product sales and R&D rose 46.10%. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-03_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation G2

- Cash conversion dipped in 2026 but remains positive. Operating cash flow was USD 72.92 million in nine months against USD 350.69 million a year earlier because working capital absorbed cash, yet last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 227.37 million is 15.18% of gross debt and capital spending is small. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51; calculation G4

- Floating-rate exposure is only half hedged. Collars with a 5.25% cap cover 49.61% of principal, the three-month Term SOFR rate was 4.07% at 2026-09-30, and cash interest paid is not stated, so coverage can be judged only from interest expense. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation G3; calculation G8

- Financial policy is creditor-neutral so far. No dividend has been paid to date, repurchases were small and have stopped, and the acquisition was funded without a sponsor, but legal capacity under the credit agreement is not established. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30

runs.text: Strengths, ranked. First, the maturity profile and cash leave no refinancing event before 2031: principal due before 2031 is USD 164.19 million against cash of USD 631.31 million, so debt service is met from cash and operations through the expiry window. Second, the product base is broader than a single asset, with four products at 16.51% to 26.62% of nine-month 2026 revenue and legacy product sales up 8.28% over nine months, so a problem in one product does not remove most of the cash flow. Third, ARISTADA and LYBALVI patents run to 2039 and 2041 and LUMRYZ patents to 2037, so the newer products outlast the 2029 and 2030 expiries. Fourth, financial policy has been creditor-neutral: no dividend to date, repurchases paused and USD 172.3 million of authorisation unused, which keeps cash for debt service. Fifth, capital intensity is low, with capital spending of USD 15.64 million in nine months against operating cash flow of USD 72.92 million, so free cash flow reaches debt service without large reinvestment. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_alks-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 132; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation G6; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Weaknesses, ranked. First, leverage rose from nil to USD 1,497.73 million of secured floating-rate debt, so reported net leverage of 5.93x leaves little room for an earnings shortfall. Second, the exposed share of revenue is 31.87%, the VIVITROL product and the INVEGA royalties, which face a 2029 patent expiry and a 2030 royalty end before the 2031 maturities. Third, the margin is compressing: the adjusted margin fell 2.11 percentage points over nine months and the deduction rate is 46.6%, so revenue growth is not reaching EBITDA. Fourth, there is no committed liquidity backstop and no covenant transparency, so liquidity is cash only and headroom cannot be tested. Fifth, intangible assets and goodwill exceed shareholders' equity by USD 469.56 million and pipeline spending is rising, so asset value and cash use both depend on LUMRYZ and the orexin programmes delivering. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation G1; calculation G2; calculation G5

runs.text: The only material transaction in the period is the acquisition of Avadel Pharmaceuticals plc, agreed on 2025-10-22 and completed on 2026-02-12 at USD 21.00 per share in cash plus a contingent value right of up to USD 1.50 per share. Preliminary consideration is USD 2,306.920 million, of which USD 2,199.207 million was paid in cash and USD 107.713 million is the value of the contingent value right; the issuer allocated USD 1,768.600 million to LUMRYZ, USD 26.300 million to an in-process project and USD 509.492 million to goodwill. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 57

The new debt is one senior secured credit agreement of 2026-02-12 with a term loan A of up to USD 750.0 million due 2031-02-12 and a term loan B of up to USD 775.0 million due 2031-08-12, both drawn in full for USD 1,525.0 million, with subsidiary guarantors and a lien on substantially all assets; a bridge facility of about USD 1.5 billion was terminated undrawn on the same day and USD 731.2 million of cash had been escrowed at year-end 2025. On 2026-08-12 an amendment cut the term loan A margin by 0.75 percentage points and the term loan B margin by 0.50 percentage points, and in October 2026 two zero-cost interest rate collars with a cap of 5.25% were added; no bonds were issued and no new debt followed after 2026-09-30. fields.value: Liquidity is cash-based: cash and cash equivalents are USD 631.31 million, with a further USD 156.26 million of investments that the issuer counts in its broader measure, and no undrawn committed facility is described in the sources. fields.value: Business and governance review of Alkermes plc. (issuer id alks), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the transaction, business and revenue model, ownership, operating model, governance and sponsor behaviour that matter to a creditor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Alkermes is a listed specialty neuroscience company with no sponsor identified in the sources, and its creditors depend on four US-marketed products and royalty streams that face patent, royalty and exclusivity expiries in 2029 and 2030. The Avadel acquisition added LUMRYZ and secured floating-rate debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business risk is moderate: four products supply 85.25% of nine-month 2026 revenue, VIVITROL alone 26.62%, and sales deductions absorb 46.6% of gross product sales, so payer policy moves earnings more than volume does. Governance shows no documented extraction, but legal capacity under the credit agreement is not established because that agreement was not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation D1; calculation D2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue durability is the central business risk because expiries cluster in 2029 and 2030 on the largest product and on the royalty stream. VIVITROL, 26.62% of nine-month 2026 revenue, has one unexpired listed patent, which expires in 2029, and faces a direct-purchaser antitrust class action over a VIVITROL patent; the Janssen royalty on INVEGA TRINZA runs to the second quarter of 2030 and on INVEGA HAFYERA to May 2030, and Janssen supplied about 9% of FY2025 revenue; LUMRYZ's adult orphan exclusivity ends on 2030-05-01 although its patents run to 2037. ARISTADA and LYBALVI patents run to 2039 and 2041, so the near-term cliff is VIVITROL and the royalties rather than the whole portfolio.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Growth is acquisition-led and the legacy portfolio slowed in the third quarter. Product sales excluding LUMRYZ grew 3.13% in Q3 2026 against 8.28% over nine months, and the issuer says Q3 included about USD 17 million of inventory-timing and gross-to-net benefits and without them Q3 legacy sales would have been below Q3 2025 unless that quarter carried similar benefits, which the sources do not state.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-03_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation D4; calculation D7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Royalty and manufacturing revenue is shrinking and will end for the INVEGA products in 2030. It fell 9.12% over nine months to USD 201.93 million, with VUMERITY royalties down 15.01% and the long-acting INVEGA royalties down 8.14%, and Biogen may end the VUMERITY licence on 180 days' notice.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Avadel purchase was a strategic cash-and-debt-funded acquisition with no sponsor identified, and its residual risks are integration, the contingent value right and intangible-heavy assets. Preliminary consideration was USD 2,306.92 million, funded by USD 1,525.0 million of term loans and USD 731.2 million of cash escrowed at year-end 2025; the contingent value right is a cash claim of up to USD 165.7 million outside the debt, and intangible assets plus goodwill of USD 2,334.28 million exceed shareholders' equity by USD 469.56 million, so asset value rests on LUMRYZ continuing to earn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Payer exposure and reserves are large and judgemental. Medicaid rebate accruals were USD 186.1 million at year-end 2025 and USD 214.93 million at 2026-09-30, the auditors named them a critical audit matter, and Medicare Part D deductions rose because of expanded LYBALVI rebate eligibility, while LUMRYZ is outside Medicaid, so product mix will shift the deduction rate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Governance and financial policy show no documented extraction. No dividend has been paid to date, repurchases were USD 27.70 million in Q1 2026 and none followed in Q2 or Q3 with USD 172.3 million of authorisation left, the Chairman stays on after the chief executive handover on 2026-08-01, and disclosure controls were assessed as effective at 2026-09-30; creditor rights cannot be tested because the credit agreement and proxy statement were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The cost base is stepping up ahead of pipeline revenue. Nine-month R&D rose 46.10% to USD 337.39 million with the alixorexton phase 3 programme, selling and marketing rose 27.13% on the LUMRYZ organisation and general and administrative expense rose 50.97%, so the debt service capacity of 2027 depends on operating leverage arriving before the orexin programmes read out.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a moderate business-risk view is operating momentum: LYBALVI units rose 20% over nine months with prescriptions up 18% in Q3, a 6% price rise took effect in January 2026, LUMRYZ's phase 3 idiopathic hypersomnia study was positive in May 2026 and two new LUMRYZ patents granted in September and October 2026 run to 2037, and the issuer reiterated its 2026 expectations of USD 370 million to USD 410 million of adjusted EBITDA on 2026-11-03. The view would improve if LUMRYZ patient numbers keep growing from the roughly four thousand now on therapy and legacy sales growth holds as the price rise annualises. It would worsen if the paragraph IV suits on LYBALVI or the new LUMRYZ generic filing lead to earlier entry, if VIVITROL meets generic competition after 2029, or if Janssen ends its royalty before 2030, which it may do on three months' notice. The Q3 sales included about USD 17 million of favourable items, so one clean quarter would not by itself change the view.

fields.value: The only material transaction in the period is the acquisition of Avadel Pharmaceuticals plc, agreed on 2025-10-22 and completed on 2026-02-12 at USD 21.00 per share in cash plus a contingent value right of up to USD 1.50 per share. Preliminary consideration is USD 2,306.920 million, of which USD 2,199.207 million was paid in cash and USD 107.713 million is the value of the contingent value right; the issuer allocated USD 1,768.600 million to LUMRYZ, USD 26.300 million to an in-process project and USD 509.492 million to goodwill.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The new debt is one senior secured credit agreement of 2026-02-12 with a term loan A of up to USD 750.0 million due 2031-02-12 and a term loan B of up to USD 775.0 million due 2031-08-12, both drawn in full for USD 1,525.0 million, with subsidiary guarantors and a lien on substantially all assets; a bridge facility of about USD 1.5 billion was terminated undrawn on the same day and USD 731.2 million of cash had been escrowed at year-end 2025. On 2026-08-12 an amendment cut the term loan A margin by 0.75 percentage points and the term loan B margin by 0.50 percentage points, and in October 2026 two zero-cost interest rate collars with a cap of 5.25% were added; no bonds were issued and no new debt followed after 2026-09-30.

fields.value: Alkermes' fundamental credit profile is average and weaker than at year-end 2025, because net debt of USD 866.42 million is 5.93x reported last-twelve-months EBITDA after a debt-funded acquisition. Cash of USD 631.31 million, USD 164.19 million of principal due before 2031 and the absence of distributions cushion the near term, but the largest product's 2029 patent expiry and the 2030 end of the Janssen royalties arrive before USD 1,347.56 million falls due in 2031.

fields.value: The strongest evidence against an average rating of the profile is cash generation: last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 227.37 million is 15.18% of gross debt, capital spending is light, no distributions are paid, and the issuer's adjusted EBITDA grew 15.63% in nine months. The view would move toward strong if the fourth-quarter 2025 release shows adjusted EBITDA near the 2026 quarterly level, which would put adjusted net leverage well below the reported 5.93x, and if cash interest paid proves modest against that earnings base. It would move toward weak if the paragraph IV suits or the LUMRYZ generic filing bring earlier generic entry, if VIVITROL meets generic competition after 2029 while Janssen ends its royalty before 2030, if the deduction rate keeps rising from 47.7% in Q3, or if repurchases resume before debt falls.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths, ranked. First, the maturity profile and cash leave no refinancing event before 2031: principal due before 2031 is USD 164.19 million against cash of USD 631.31 million, so debt service is met from cash and operations through the expiry window. Second, the product base is broader than a single asset, with four products at 16.51% to 26.62% of nine-month 2026 revenue and legacy product sales up 8.28% over nine months, so a problem in one product does not remove most of the cash flow. Third, ARISTADA and LYBALVI patents run to 2039 and 2041 and LUMRYZ patents to 2037, so the newer products outlast the 2029 and 2030 expiries. Fourth, financial policy has been creditor-neutral: no dividend to date, repurchases paused and USD 172.3 million of authorisation unused, which keeps cash for debt service. Fifth, capital intensity is low, with capital spending of USD 15.64 million in nine months against operating cash flow of USD 72.92 million, so free cash flow reaches debt service without large reinvestment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses, ranked. First, leverage rose from nil to USD 1,497.73 million of secured floating-rate debt, so reported net leverage of 5.93x leaves little room for an earnings shortfall. Second, the exposed share of revenue is 31.87%, the VIVITROL product and the INVEGA royalties, which face a 2029 patent expiry and a 2030 royalty end before the 2031 maturities. Third, the margin is compressing: the adjusted margin fell 2.11 percentage points over nine months and the deduction rate is 46.6%, so revenue growth is not reaching EBITDA. Fourth, there is no committed liquidity backstop and no covenant transparency, so liquidity is cash only and headroom cannot be tested. Fifth, intangible assets and goodwill exceed shareholders' equity by USD 469.56 million and pipeline spending is rising, so asset value and cash use both depend on LUMRYZ and the orexin programmes delivering.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Alkermes sells four US products and earns royalties on two collaboration partners' products: VIVITROL for alcohol and opioid dependence, ARISTADA and LYBALVI for schizophrenia and bipolar I disorder, and, since the Avadel acquisition of 2026-02-12, LUMRYZ for narcolepsy; Janssen pays royalties on the INVEGA family and royalties and manufacturing fees on RISPERDAL CONSTA, and Biogen pays royalties on VUMERITY. Sales go mainly to three wholesalers, so cash flow depends on a few products, a few channels and US payers, which lowers diversification but gives clear volume and price data; the pipeline of orexin 2 receptor agonists is a growth option that consumes cash first. Cash-generation durability is therefore reasonable to 2030 and uncertain after it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_alks-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_alks-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Alkermes is a listed Irish public company with no sponsor or controlling holder identified, so financial policy is set by a board and management rather than a sponsor with an exit horizon; the only large corporate action in the period was the debt-funded Avadel purchase, and creditors rank as senior secured lenders to borrowers that are Alkermes plc, Alkermes, Inc. and Alkermes Finance LLC with subsidiary guarantors. Holder concentration, board composition and the guarantor list are not established because the proxy statement and credit agreement were not supplied, so governance risk is held at medium rather than low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue durability is mixed. Evidence: legacy product sales rose 8.28% over nine months on a 6% list price rise and unit growth, but Q3 growth slowed to 3.13% and included about USD 17 million of timing and deduction benefits, while royalty and manufacturing revenue fell 9.12%. Mechanism: deductions absorb 46.6% of gross sales, wholesaler concentration is high and each product is a US single-market franchise, so revenue is recurring and prescription-driven rather than contractual, and exposed to regulation and substitution. Implication: revenue is predictable at the product level but structurally exposed to rebate policy and to patent-led generic entry, with VIVITROL the first test in 2029.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_alks-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_alks-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended only partly. Evidence: nine-month 2026 cost of goods was 18.55% of revenue including non-cash inventory step-up amortisation, R&D was 24.64% and selling, general and administrative expense 50.45%, with R&D up 46.10% and selling and marketing up 27.13% on the LUMRYZ organisation. Mechanism: most of the cost base is commercial and development spend that does not fall with volume, so a revenue decline would deleverage margins quickly; R&D is the main discretionary lever. Implication: operating leverage works against the issuer in a downturn and the cost step-up must be matched by LUMRYZ and legacy growth to hold EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation G7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is adequate but volatile. Evidence: operating cash flow fell 79.21% to USD 72.92 million in nine months of 2026 as payables and accrued expenses fell and acquisition and interest costs rose, capital additions were only USD 15.64 million, and the 2026 reports do not state cash interest paid. Mechanism: payer reserves and the working-capital swing make quarterly cash flow noisy, and interest on USD 1,497.73 million of floating-rate debt is now a recurring claim. Implication: EBITDA reaches free cash flow because capital intensity is low, but interest is a new leakage whose cash amount is not established, and capital spending flexibility adds little because the base is small.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alks-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51; calculation G4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense and product-specific: ARISTADA, the INVEGA products and RISPERDAL CONSTA compete with other long-acting injectables, LYBALVI with oral antipsychotics such as CAPLYTA, REXULTI, VRAYLAR and COBENFY, VIVITROL with buprenorphine products and generics, and LUMRYZ with twice-nightly oxybates and wake-promoting agents, so share and price pressure fall mostly on net price rather than on volume, which the 46.6% deduction rate already shows. Buyer power is high because three wholesalers take 71% to 96% of each product's gross sales and payers set rebates, which squeezes net price. Substitutes and new entrants are the generic filings against LYBALVI and LUMRYZ, which the patent estate and 30-month stays delay but do not remove. Supplier power is limited for the legacy products made at the Ohio plant, higher for LUMRYZ because third parties make it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Policy is a material credit factor. Evidence: the annual report describes the 2025 executive order on most-favoured-nation pricing and three payment models, including a Medicare Part D rebate programme proposed from 2027-01-01 and a voluntary Medicaid model launched in January 2026, and the issuer's Part D deductions already rose because of expanded LYBALVI rebate eligibility. Mechanism: mandatory or supplemental rebates cut net price on a product whose gross sales are already 46.6% deducted. Implication: policy is a second-order downside to the 2029 and 2030 expiries, which is why deduction rate is a monitoring trigger. Macro, currency and technology factors do not appear to be primary credit drivers: the issuer reports no material change in its currency exposure, which arises from euro royalties offset by euro costs in Ireland.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths: cash of USD 631.31 million, light amortisation, a four-product base, patents to 2039 and 2041 on ARISTADA and LYBALVI, and no distributions. Weaknesses: acquisition leverage, a 2031 maturity wall, a declining royalty stream, a rising deduction rate and no covenant transparency. Opportunities that could improve credit quality: LUMRYZ patients and its idiopathic hypersomnia label expansion, orexin programme readouts, and further margin cuts at the next amendment. Threats that could weaken it: generic entry on VIVITROL after 2029, loss of the Janssen royalty by 2030, a paragraph IV outcome on LYBALVI or LUMRYZ, and mandatory rebate models.

fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are LUMRYZ patient growth from roughly four thousand now on therapy, the 6% price rise, LYBALVI prescriptions growing 18%, and lower interest cost after the margin cut; the headwinds are the Q3 one-offs that will not repeat, the deduction rate and higher R&D for the phase 3 programmes. The company expects 2026 revenue of USD 1,730 million to USD 1,840 million and adjusted EBITDA of USD 370 million to USD 410 million, which implies fourth-quarter revenue of USD 360.95 million to USD 470.95 million and fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA of only USD 30.46 million to USD 70.46 million against USD 120.07 million in Q3, so either the expectations are cautious or a heavy fourth-quarter cost step-up is planned. Over three to five years the expiries of 2029 and 2030 dominate: roughly a third of revenue is exposed while the orexin pipeline would need to be approved and launched to replace it, and the 2031 maturities fall at the end of that window. Sector tailwinds are demand for long-acting psychiatric and sleep products; sector headwinds are US drug pricing policy and generic challenges.

fields.value: The issuer-specific downside begins in 2029 with generic competition for VIVITROL, the largest product at 26.62% of nine-month revenue, followed in 2030 by the end of the Janssen royalty on the INVEGA products and of LUMRYZ's adult orphan exclusivity. The first operational break is volume and price loss on VIVITROL, which also faces an antitrust class action over a patent, and the end of high-margin royalty income. Revenue falls by part of the 31.87% that is directly exposed; because commercial and R&D spending is largely fixed, EBITDA falls by more than revenue, and free cash flow, which was USD 227.37 million over the last twelve months, falls with it while interest on the floating-rate term loans continues. Liquidity is not the first casualty: cash of USD 631.31 million and principal of only USD 164.19 million due before 2031 mean the company can fund the expiry window, and management can cut R&D, stop repurchases and repay debt from cash. Leverage is the consequence: lower EBITDA over unchanged debt raises net leverage above 5.93x just as USD 1,347.56 million of term loans needs refinancing in 2031, so resilience is sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2030 but the refinancing is the pressure point. Observable triggers are generic filings or approvals for VIVITROL, rulings in the LYBALVI and LUMRYZ suits, any Janssen termination notice, the deduction rate and cash balance.

Cash-flow durability appears adequate to 2030 and not fully assessable after it. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on how much of the exposed revenue is replaced by LUMRYZ and the orexin programmes before USD 1,347.56 million of term loans falls due in 2031. The primary downside path is generic entry for VIVITROL and the end of the Janssen royalties meeting that refinancing. Further analysis would require cash interest paid, the covenant levels, the fourth-quarter 2025 adjusted EBITDA and any rating. Top risk: refinancing the 2031 term loans after the 2029 and 2030 expiries.
